title: BPSC TRE 4.0 Day 01 Complete Practice Test (50 Questions)

sections.name: Part II: General Studies & Bihar Special (सामान्य अध्ययन)
Part IV: Class 9–10 Secondary Mathematics (माध्यमिक गणित)

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: What is the correct grammatical Sandhi-Vichhed (disjunction) of the Sanskrit loanword 'Ujjwal' (उज्ज्वल)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct Sandhi-Vichhed is 'Ut + Jwal' (उत् + ज्वल = उज्ज्वल).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Consonant Sandhi (व्यंजन संधि) Rule: When 't' (त्) or 'd' (द्) is followed by 'j' (ज्) or 'jh' (झ्), the preceding 't/d' assimilates into 'j' (ज्).
aiDeepSolution.trick: In 'Ujjwal', both 'j' letters are half (consonant cluster j + j + v + l). This is a frequent BPSC question in both Sandhi and orthography (spelling test).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Students often pick 'Ud + Jwal' due to colloquial Hindi variations, but according to Paninian Sanskrit grammar and official BPSC answer keys, 'Ut' is the standard prefix.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which type of compound (Samas) is present in the compound word 'Yathashakti' (यथाशक्ति)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Yathashakti' is an authentic example of Avyayibhav Samas (अव्ययीभाव समास).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Avyayibhav Samas: A compound where the initial constituent is an Indeclinable/Prefix (Avyaya) and is the principal element, causing the whole compound to function adverbially.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Look for prefixes like 'Yatha-', 'Prati-', 'Be-', 'Ba-', 'Bhar-', 'Anu-'. Yathashakti literally translates to 'according to one's capacity' (शक्ति के अनुसार).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Tatpurush involves elision of case endings (Karak), whereas here 'Yatha' is an indeclinable modifier.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which of the following spellings is orthographically correct in Hindi?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The authentic feminine form of 'Kavi' is 'Kavayitri' (कवयित्री).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Feminine noun formation: In Hindi/Sanskrit, the feminine counterpart of Kavi is derived as Kav + ayitri, not Kavi + yatri.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Remember the syllable pattern: Ka - va - yi - tree (no vowel mark on 'va').
aiDeepSolution.trap: Most candidates intuitively place a short 'i' on 'v' (*Kaviyatri), which is an erroneous hypercorrection.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which prefix (Upasarg) is used in the compound word 'Atyant' (अत्यंत)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The prefix is 'Ati' (अति). Ati + Ant = Atyant (Yan vowel Sandhi).

aiDeepSolution.concept: A prefix (Upasarg) is an affix placed at the beginning of a root word. Here, 'i' of Ati combines with 'a' of Ant to form 'y' via Yan Sandhi rules.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Split the word by Sandhi: Ati + Ant = Atyant. Hence the root prefix is 'Ati'.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often superficially look at the first two letters and pick 'Atya', which is not a standard prefix.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the correct verb to fill in the blank:
'Neither the teacher nor the students _______ present in the seminar yesterday.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The grammatically correct verb is 'were'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Rule of Proximity: When two subjects are connected by correlative conjunctions 'Neither...nor' or 'Either...or', the finite verb agrees in number and person with the closest subject.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Identify the noun adjacent to the blank: 'students' (plural) -> requires plural past verb 'were' (time marker is 'yesterday').
aiDeepSolution.trap: If the sentence were inverted ('Neither the students nor the teacher...'), the verb would be singular ('was'). Here 'students' governs the verb.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the appropriate article to fill in the blank:
'He is _______ European scholar whom we met in Patna.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct indefinite article is 'a'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Indefinite article choice ('a' vs 'an') is strictly determined by the initial phonetic sound of the following word, not the orthographic letter. 'European' begins with the consonant glide /juː/ (like 'you').
aiDeepSolution.trick: Words like 'a European', 'a university', 'a unicorn', 'a one-rupee note' all take 'a' because they begin with consonant phonemes /j/ or /w/.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not mechanically pick 'an' merely because the word opens with vowel letter 'E'.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Complete the sentence with the correct conditional structure:
'If the candidate _______ harder, he would have cleared the BPSC examination.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct past perfect conditional form is 'had worked'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Third Conditional (Past Unreal Condition): If + Past Perfect (had + V3), Subject + would have + Past Participle (V3).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Notice 'would have cleared' in the main clause. It strictly pairs with 'had + V3' in the If-clause.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Using 'would have worked' in the If-clause is a common error (Conditionals never take 'would' in the If-clause).

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the correct preposition to fill in the blank:
'The live online lecture is scheduled to start _______ 8:30 AM sharp.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct preposition for a precise point of clock time is 'at'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Prepositions of Time: Use 'at' for precise clock times and specific points of day (at 8:30 AM, at noon, at midnight).
aiDeepSolution.trick: 'At' = clock time | 'On' = days and dates | 'In' = months, years, and seasons.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not use 'in' or 'on' for specific hour markers.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: Where did the 1857 Revolt in Bihar initially break out on 12 June 1857?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 1857 revolt in Bihar initially broke out on 12 June 1857 in Rohini village (now in Deoghar district, Jharkhand) by the soldiers of the 32nd Native Infantry Regiment.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Initial spark of 1857 in Bihar took place at Rohini village, where Lieutenant Norman Leslie was killed by mutinous soldiers.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Chronology: Rohini (12 June) ⟶ Patna (3 July) ⟶ Danapur (25 July) ⟶ Jagdishpur (26 July).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Most candidates mark Danapur or Jagdishpur, which occurred later in July 1857.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: Who led the 1857 uprising in Patna City on 3 July 1857?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The uprising in Patna City was led by Pir Ali Khan, a local bookseller, on 3 July 1857.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Pir Ali Khan mobilized the local masses in Patna. In the ensuing clash, British Opium Agent Dr. R. Lyell was killed. Commissioner William Tayler suppressed the revolt and Pir Ali was publicly executed.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Patna City = Pir Ali Khan (Bookseller). Jagdishpur = Babu Kunwar Singh.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing the urban Patna revolt with the Arrah/Jagdishpur rebellion led by Kunwar Singh.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: At the age of nearly 80, which eminent leader from Jagdishpur spearheaded the 1857 rebellion and defeated British forces under Captain Dunbar and Le Grand?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Babu Veer Kunwar Singh, the zamindar of Jagdishpur (Arrah), led the 1857 rebellion in Bihar.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Kunwar Singh assumed leadership after the Danapur sepoy revolt on 25 July 1857. He defeated Dunbar near Arrah and Le Grand near Jagdishpur before succumbing to injuries on 26 April 1858.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Look for keywords 'Jagdishpur' and '80 years old' ⟶ Babu Veer Kunwar Singh.
aiDeepSolution.trap: His younger brother Amar Singh continued the guerrilla struggle after his death from the Kaimur Hills.

questions.subject: National Movement
questions.question: What proportion of land was compulsorily reserved for indigo cultivation under the Tinkathia system in Champaran?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Under the Tinkathia system, tenant farmers were legally compelled by European planters to cultivate indigo on 3/20th (3 kathas per bigha) of their most fertile land.

aiDeepSolution.concept: 1 Bigha = 20 Kathas in Bihar. 'Tin-kathia' literally means 3 kathas out of 20 kathas (3/20th).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Tinkathia = 3 kathas out of 1 Bigha (20 Kathas) = 3/20.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse 3/20 with 3/10 or 1/3.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: Who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi during the 1916 Lucknow Congress Session to visit Champaran and investigate the plight of indigo cultivators?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Rajkumar Shukla, a farmer from Murli Bharhawa in Champaran, persistently pursued Mahatma Gandhi and persuaded him at the Lucknow Session (1916).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Rajkumar Shukla represented the suffering peasantry of Champaran. Gandhi accompanied him to Patna, Muzaffarpur, and finally arrived in Champaran in April 1917.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Lucknow Congress 1916 invitation = Rajkumar Shukla.
aiDeepSolution.trap: While Rajendra Prasad and Brajkishore Prasad were key associates during the inquiry, the primary initiator who brought Gandhi was Rajkumar Shukla.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: As an outcome of the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), what percentage of the illegally extorted dues did European planters agree to refund?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: European planters agreed to refund exactly 25% of the money they had illegally extorted from the ryots.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Gandhi compromised on a 25% refund to break the prestige and moral dominance of the British planters. The Tinkathia system was formally abolished by the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Gandhi accepted 25% refund because the planters' prestige was shattered more than the monetary concession.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often assume full refund (100%) or half (50%). The exact figure is 25%.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: What is the total length of the River Ganga within the geographic territory of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The total length of the Ganga river in Bihar is 445 km, passing through 12 districts.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Ganga has a total length of 2,525 km in India. In Bihar, its stretch is 445 km, entering at Chausa (Buxar) and exiting at Manihari (Katihar). It has its longest stretch in Patna district (~99 km).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Remember 445 km (exactly 12 districts). Patna has the longest stretch (~99 km).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse the Bihar length (445 km) with the West Bengal or UP stretches.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: Near which historic location does the River Ganga enter the state of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Ganga enters Bihar near Chausa in Buxar district.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Ganga enters Bihar at Chausa (Buxar) and exits near Manihari (Katihar).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Entry = Chausa (Buxar) | Exit = Manihari (Katihar).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Valmikinagar is the entry point of the Gandak river, not the Ganga.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: At which confluence point does the Kosi River ('Sorrow of Bihar') merge into the River Ganga?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Kosi River merges into the Ganga at Kursela in Katihar district.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Kosi River originates as Saptakoshi in Nepal, enters Bihar at Supaul, and flows through Saharsa and Madhepura to merge with the Ganga at Kursela (Katihar).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Kosi ⟶ Kursela (K-K pairing).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Pahleza is the confluence of Gandak, while Maner is the confluence of Son.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: Which major south-bank peninsular tributary of the Ganga originates from the Amarkantak Plateau and joins the Ganga near Maner in Patna district?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Son River originates from the Amarkantak plateau (Madhya Pradesh) and joins the Ganga near Maner (Patna).

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Son River enters Bihar at Rohtas district, flows between Rohtas/Bhojpur and Aurangabad/Arwal, and joins the Ganga near Maner.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Son River: Origin = Amarkantak, Entry in Bihar = Rohtas, Confluence = Maner (Patna).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Punpun meets the Ganga at Fatuha, not Maner.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: At which place does the Punpun River join the River Ganga?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Punpun River joins the Ganga at Fatuha (east of Patna).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Originating in the Chota Nagpur Plateau of Jharkhand, the Punpun flows through Aurangabad, Arwal, and Patna before meeting the Ganga at Fatuha.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Punpun meets Ganga at Fatuha.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Chhapra is where the Ghaghara meets the Ganga.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: What is the total geographical area of the state of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The total geographical area of Bihar is 94,163 square kilometers, accounting for 2.86% of India's total geographical area (12th largest state by area).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Area = 94,163 sq km. North-to-South span = 345 km. East-to-West span = 483 km.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Mnemonic: 94-163 (94 thousand, 163).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse the area with population percentages (population is 8.6% of India, 3rd largest).

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: In the agricultural plains of South Bihar, the older alluvium (Bangar) is locally known by which name?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In South Bihar, older alluvium (Bangar) is locally referred to as 'Karail-Kewal' soil.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Karail-Kewal soil is characterized by heavy clay, high water retention, neutral to slightly alkaline pH, and presence of calcareous kankar nodules.
aiDeepSolution.trick: South Bihar Older Alluvium = Karail-Kewal. Newer Alluvium = Khadar.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Terai soil is found in the northern Himalayan border belt of West Champaran, Kishanganj.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: On which historic date did the Constituent Assembly of India adopt, enact, and give to themselves the Constitution of India?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas) and came into full legal enforcement on 26 January 1950.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Preamble explicitly states: 'In our Constituent Assembly this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do hereby Adopt, Enact and Give to Ourselves this Constitution.'
aiDeepSolution.trick: Adopted = 26 Nov 1949. Enforced (Republic Day) = 26 Jan 1950.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often choose 26 January 1950, which is the date of commencement/enforcement, not adoption.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7–8 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the additive inverse of the rational number -7/19?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The additive inverse of -7/19 is 7/19, because (-7/19) + (7/19) = 0.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Additive inverse of a is -a such that a + (-a) = 0 (the additive identity).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Just invert the sign: negative becomes positive, positive becomes negative.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not flip numerator and denominator (that is the reciprocal / multiplicative inverse).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7–8 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of -13/17?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The multiplicative inverse of -13/17 is -17/13, because (-13/17) × (-17/13) = 1.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Multiplicative inverse of a/b is b/a such that (a/b) × (b/a) = 1. The algebraic sign remains unchanged.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Reciprocal flips the fraction upside down while keeping the negative sign.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Changing the sign to positive is an error; that confuses it with additive inverse.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 8 Mathematics
questions.question: For any non-zero rational number x, what is the product of its additive inverse and its multiplicative inverse?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The additive inverse is -x and the multiplicative inverse is 1/x. Their product is (-x) × (1/x) = -1.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Universal algebraic identity: Additive Inverse × Multiplicative Inverse = (-x) × (1/x) = -1 for any x ≠ 0.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Take any sample number, e.g., 5: Additive inv = -5, Multiplicative inv = 1/5. Product = -5 × 1/5 = -1.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Thinking the product cancels out to positive +1.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6–8 Mathematics
questions.question: If the 6-digit number 473x24 is divisible by 9, what is the single-digit value of x?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sum of digits = 4 + 7 + 3 + x + 2 + 4 = 20 + x. The next multiple of 9 is 27, so 20 + x = 27 ⟹ x = 7.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Divisibility rule for 9: A number is divisible by 9 if and only if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 9.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Sum known digits: 4 + 7 + 3 + 2 + 4 = 20. Nearest multiple of 9 > 20 is 27. x = 27 - 20 = 7.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Picking 5 gives sum 25, which is not divisible by 9.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6–8 Mathematics
questions.question: If the 7-digit number 853x412 is completely divisible by 11, what is the value of digit x?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sum of odd-position digits = 2 + 4 + 3 + 8 = 17. Sum of even-position digits = 1 + x + 5 = 6 + x. Difference = 17 - (6 + x) = 11 - x. For divisibility by 11, 11 - x must be a multiple of 11 ⟹ x = 0. Since 0 is not listed in options (A, B, C), the correct BPSC answer is 'None of the above'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Divisibility rule for 11: Difference between the sum of digits in odd places and even places must be either 0 or a multiple of 11.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Calculate: Sum(Odd) - Sum(Even) = 17 - (6 + x) = 11 - x. For a single digit (0-9), only x = 0 satisfies this condition.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often hesitate to choose 'None of the above' (Option E) even when their calculation is correct. BPSC frequently makes Option E the correct answer!

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6 Mathematics
questions.question: Three bells toll at intervals of 12, 15, and 18 seconds respectively. If they toll together now, after how many minutes will they next toll together?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 15, 18) = 180 seconds. In minutes: 180 / 60 = 3 minutes.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Simultaneous recurring events occur at the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their individual time periods.
aiDeepSolution.trick: 12 = 2² × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 18 = 2 × 3². LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180 seconds. Convert to minutes: 180 / 60 = 3 minutes.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates find 180 and forget to convert seconds into minutes.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of the fractions 2/3, 4/9, and 5/6?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) / (HCF of denominators) = LCM(2, 4, 5) / HCF(3, 9, 6) = 20 / 3.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Standard Fraction Formula: LCM(Fractions) = LCM(Numerators) / HCF(Denominators).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Numerators = 2, 4, 5 ⟶ LCM = 20. Denominators = 3, 9, 6 ⟶ HCF = 3. Result = 20/3.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Inverting the formula (e.g., finding HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators, which gives HCF, not LCM).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6 Science
questions.question: In a laboratory test, when a few drops of dilute Iodine solution are added to a crushed food sample, it turns Blue-Black. This confirms the presence of which nutrient?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A blue-black coloration with dilute Iodine solution confirms the presence of starch.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Iodine intercalates into the helical amylose structure of starch, producing a characteristic deep blue-black charge-transfer complex.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Iodine ⟶ Blue-Black = Starch.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Proteins give violet with Biuret test, not blue-black with iodine.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6 Science
questions.question: Which chemical reagents are used in the Biuret test to confirm the presence of proteins in food?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Copper Sulphate (CuSO4) and Caustic Soda (NaOH) are added to test for proteins, producing a violet color.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Biuret reaction: Cu²⁺ ions form a violet coordination complex with peptide bonds in alkaline (NaOH) medium.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Protein Test = CuSO4 + NaOH ⟶ Violet color.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing CuSO4 with FeSO4 or iodine.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6–7 Science
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins are completely water-soluble and must be regularly supplied in the daily diet?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Vitamin B-complex and Vitamin C are water-soluble vitamins, excreted regularly through urine.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vitamins are classified into: Fat-soluble (K, E, D, A) stored in liver/adipose tissue; and Water-soluble (B-complex, C) which cannot be stored in the body.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Mnemonic: 'K-E-D-A' is fat-soluble. 'B and C' are water-soluble.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Vitamins A, D, E, K are fat-soluble and excess can cause hypervitaminosis.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7 Science
questions.question: If two plane mirrors are placed inclined at an angle of 60° to each other, how many images of an object placed between them will be formed?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The formula is n = (360° / θ) - 1 when 360/θ is an even integer. Here n = (360 / 60) - 1 = 6 - 1 = 5 images.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Number of images between inclined plane mirrors: When 360/θ is even, n = (360/θ) - 1 regardless of object position.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Forgetting to subtract 1 and answering 6.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7–8 Science
questions.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a concave mirror to obtain a virtual, erect, and magnified image?
options: Between the Focus (F) and Centre of Curvature (C)
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When an object is placed between the Pole (P) and Focus (F) of a concave mirror, the reflected rays diverge and appear to meet behind the mirror, forming a virtual, erect, and magnified image.

aiDeepSolution.concept: In all other positions, a concave mirror forms a real and inverted image. Only when placed between P and F does it form a virtual, erect, and enlarged image (principle of dentist mirrors).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Dentist Mirror Case: Between P and F ⟶ Virtual, Erect, Enlarged.
aiDeepSolution.trap: At C it forms real, inverted, same size image. Between F and C it forms real, inverted, magnified image.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7 Science
questions.source: NCERT Transportation in Animals and Plants
questions.question: Which plant vascular tissue is responsible for the bidirectional translocation of synthesized food (sucrose) from leaves to other storage organs?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Phloem translocates organic nutrients (food/sugars) bidirectionally throughout the plant.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Phloem transports food (sucrose) in both upward and downward directions (bidirectional translocation) using energy (ATP). Xylem conducts water and minerals unidirectionally upwards.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Phloem = Food (bidirectional) | Xylem = Water/Jal (unidirectional).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing Xylem (water) with Phloem (food).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 8 Science
questions.question: If the amplitude of a sound wave is tripled, by what factor will the loudness of the sound increase?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Loudness of sound is directly proportional to the square of its amplitude: Loudness ∝ (Amplitude)². When amplitude is tripled (3×), loudness increases by 3² = 9 times.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Physics of Sound: Loudness ∝ A². Pitch is determined by frequency, whereas loudness/intensity is determined by amplitude squared.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Loudness ∝ A² ⟶ (3)² = 9 times.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Assuming linear relationship (3 times).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, every composite number can be factorized as a product of prime numbers in a manner that is:
options: Unique, apart from the order in which prime factors occur
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite number can be uniquely expressed as a product of primes, up to the order of factors.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Theorem 1.2 (NCERT Class 10): Every composite number can be factored uniquely as a product of primes, apart from the order in which the prime factors occur.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Fundamental Theorem = Unique Prime Factorization.
aiDeepSolution.trap: The order can change (e.g., 2 × 3 = 3 × 2), but the set of prime factors and their multiplicities are strictly unique.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: A rational number p/q in simplest form (gcd(p, q) = 1) has a terminating decimal expansion if and only if the prime factorisation of q contains:
options: Only primes of the form 2^n · 5^m (n, m non-negative integers)
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A rational number has a terminating decimal expansion if and only if the denominator q is of the form 2^n · 5^m, where n and m are non-negative integers.

aiDeepSolution.concept: NCERT Theorem: Let x = p/q be a rational number such that prime factorisation of q is of the form 2^n · 5^m. Then x has a terminating decimal expansion.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Terminating decimal denominator must ONLY have factors of 2 and/or 5.
aiDeepSolution.trap: If any other prime (like 3, 7, 11) is present in the reduced denominator, the decimal is non-terminating repeating.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: After how many decimal places will the decimal expansion of 13 / 1250 terminate?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 1250 = 2^1 × 5^4. The decimal expansion terminates after max(1, 4) = 4 decimal places.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The decimal expansion of p / (2^n · 5^m) terminates after exactly max(n, m) places.
aiDeepSolution.trick: 1250 = 2 × 625 = 2^1 × 5^4. The highest power between 1 and 4 is 4. Hence, terminates after 4 places (0.0104).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Counting only the power of 2 or taking the sum 1+4=5.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the geometric shape of the graph of the quadratic polynomial P(x) = ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The graph of a quadratic polynomial P(x) = ax² + bx + c is a Parabola (opening upward if a > 0, downward if a < 0).

aiDeepSolution.concept: The graph of y = ax² + bx + c is a parabola. It intersects the x-axis at at most 2 points, corresponding to its real zeros.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Linear = Straight line | Quadratic = Parabola.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Parabolas are not hyperbolas or circles.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If α and β are the zeros of the quadratic polynomial P(x) = 3x² - 5x - 2, what is the sum of its zeros (α + β)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: By Vieta's formulas, sum of zeros α + β = -b/a = -(-5)/3 = 5/3.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vieta's formula for quadratic ax² + bx + c: Sum of roots α + β = -b/a.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Forgetting the negative sign in -b/a and answering -5/3.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If α and β are the zeros of the quadratic polynomial P(x) = 2x² + 7x + 5, what is the product of its zeros (αβ)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Product of zeros αβ = c/a = 5/2.

aiDeepSolution.concept: For ax² + bx + c, product of zeros is αβ = c/a.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Putting a negative sign on c/a.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If α and β are the zeros of the polynomial P(x) = ax² + bx + c (a, c ≠ 0), what is the value of (1/α + 1/β)?
options: More than one of the above

aiDeepSolution.concept: Sum of reciprocals: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ). Since α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a, the ratio is (-b/a)/(c/a) = -b/c.
aiDeepSolution.trick: 1/α + 1/β is always equal to -b/c. Direct exam shortcut!
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing with -b/a or +b/c.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If in the quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c, all three coefficients a, b, and c are positive (a > 0, b > 0, c > 0), then both its zeros are:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sum of zeros = -b/a < 0 (negative) and Product of zeros = c/a > 0 (positive). Since the product is positive, both roots have the same sign. Since their sum is negative, both zeros must be strictly negative.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Sign analysis of quadratic roots: αβ = c/a > 0 means roots have identical signs. α + β = -b/a < 0 means their sum is negative. Therefore, both roots must be negative.
aiDeepSolution.trick: All positive coefficients ⟶ both roots are negative.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Assuming positive coefficients yield positive roots.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If one of the zeros of the cubic polynomial P(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d is 0, what is the product of the other two zeros?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: For a cubic polynomial, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a. If one zero is 0 (say γ = 0), then αβ + 0 + 0 = c/a ⟹ αβ = c/a.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vieta's relations for cubic: α + β + γ = -b/a, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a, αβγ = -d/a. If γ = 0, then the sum of pairwise products simplifies directly to αβ = c/a.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Put γ = 0 into αβ + βγ + γα = c/a ⟶ αβ = c/a.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing with -d/a.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 9 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when the polynomial P(x) = 2x³ - 3x² + 4x - 5 is divided by (x - 2)?
options: More than one of the above

aiDeepSolution.concept: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - a), the remainder is P(a).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Performing long polynomial division when direct substitution takes 10 seconds.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 9 Mathematics
questions.question: According to the Factor Theorem, a linear polynomial (x - a) is a factor of polynomial P(x) if and only if:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: (x - a) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(a) = 0.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Factor Theorem is a corollary of the Remainder Theorem: P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + P(a). If remainder P(a) = 0, then (x - a) is a factor.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Factor condition = Remainder P(a) is zero.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing P(a) = 0 with P(0) = a.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.source: NCERT Chapter 3 Pair of Linear Equations
questions.question: Under which condition does a pair of linear equations a1·x + b1·y + c1 = 0 and a2·x + b2·y + c2 = 0 represent two intersecting straight lines with a UNIQUE solution?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A pair of linear equations has a unique solution (intersecting lines) if and only if a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Linear system geometric conditions: 1. Unique solution (intersecting) ⟶ a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2. 2. Infinitely many (coincident) ⟶ a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2. 3. No solution (parallel) ⟶ a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Unique solution = Slopes are unequal = a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing with the condition for coincident or parallel lines.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: For what value of k will the system of equations 2x + 3y = 7 and (k - 1)x + (k + 2)y = 3k have INFINITELY MANY solutions?
options: More than one of the above

aiDeepSolution.concept: Infinitely many solutions condition: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Cross multiply 2(k+2) = 3(k-1) ⟶ 2k + 4 = 3k - 3 ⟶ k = 7. Verify: 2/6 = 3/9 = 7/21 = 1/3 (holds true!).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Not verifying with the constant ratio c1/c2.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: A motor boat can travel at 15 km/h in still water. If the river stream flows at 3 km/h, what is the time taken by the boat to travel 36 km downstream?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h. Time taken = Distance / Speed = 36 / 18 = 2 hours.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Boat & Stream Kinematics: Downstream speed = u + v, Upstream speed = u - v.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Downstream = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h. Time = 36 / 18 = 2 hours.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Using upstream speed (15 - 3 = 12 km/h ⟶ 36/12 = 3 hours) instead of downstream.
